reason: The recovered primary Main Theorem on printed page 458 is precise, but it is not the intake's combined root. It gives the coefficient-defined lift F_t, modularity at a certain level N_t, and cuspidality only when k is at least 5. It does not itself state general Hecke compatibility. The all-prime eigenform and Euler-product branch is distributed across Corollary 1.8, Theorem 1.9, and the corollary on pages 458-459. Therefore selecting the Main Theorem alone would narrow the intake, while conjoining additional results without an approved crosswalk would invent a new root. Independently, the pinned Lean closure lacks native half-integral-weight modular-form, theta-multiplier slash-action, and source Hecke-operator interfaces. The historical StatementShape uses unconstrained proposition fields and omits the squarefree parameter and coefficient equality, so it cannot supply exact-statement credit.

source_boundary.main_theorem_pinpoint: Printed page 458, Section 3 Main Theorem: odd k at least 3; positive N divisible by 4; character chi modulo N; f in S_k(N, chi); positive squarefree t; chi_t and A_t defined by explicit Kronecker-symbol and Dirichlet-series formulas; an eigenfunction premise at specified prime factors of N; F_t in the integral-weight modular-form space of weight k-1, level N_t, character chi^2; cuspidality only for k at least 5.
source_boundary.distributed_hecke_branch: Corollary 1.8 and Theorem 1.9 on printed pages 451-453 give coefficient recurrences and an Euler product under Hecke-eigenfunction hypotheses; the corollary spanning printed pages 458-459 combines the Main Theorem with Theorem 1.9. No single inspected result literally matches the intake's unconditional-sounding Hecke-compatibility sentence.
source_boundary.source_acceptance_boundary: Exact transcription review, notation and definition genealogy, proposition selection or composition, correction and errata disposition, lawful immutable preservation, and independent review remain open. H0 is not claimed.

source_fidelity_conflicts: The intake says cuspidal input yields a cuspidal lift, but the Main Theorem's cusp conclusion requires k at least 5; the weight-3 branch needs a distinct refinement and scope decision.

The intake requires Hecke compatibility, while the page-458 Main Theorem uses a restricted eigenfunction hypothesis and states modularity and conditional cuspidality rather than a general operator-commutation conclusion.
The Main Theorem leaves N_t as a certain positive integer, later described by Proposition 3.7; treating the target level as a simpler fixed level requires additional hypotheses or a later refinement.
The theorem-family label does not decide whether the root is the t-indexed Main Theorem, the all-prime corollary, an operator-compatibility theorem, or a reviewed conjunction.
